subject.title: Explore deterministic profiling gates for Crabbox runs

question: Should Crabbox own deterministic fuel/instruction budget gates as a core run-evidence feature, and if so which first metric, workload, runtime boundary, and provider capability shape should define v1?
rationale: Current main documents the contract but deliberately leaves runtime, security, provider capability, CLI flags, and budget semantics as future work; those are product and architecture choices rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow v1
options.body: Define one deterministic metric, one real wasm-compilable proving workload, a provider-neutral timing/budget schema, and a runtime security boundary before implementation.

options.title: Keep as research
options.body: Leave the issue open as a design placeholder until a real Crabbox workload proves the value of deterministic counters.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide perf budget gates should live outside Crabbox core or as an external provider/plugin surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow v1
recommendation.body: Define one deterministic metric, one real wasm-compilable proving workload, a provider-neutral timing/budget schema, and a runtime security boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the most visible recent owner for the timing/provider code and already commented that this remains the canonical product question.
